body.statement: For every \(L\geq3\), every \((\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\Delta_L^2\), and every \(0<\alpha<1\), the shortest arbitrary and interval-valid sets satisfy \[\frac{I^*}{k^*}\leq\frac{2L-1}{3},\qquad I^*-k^*\leq2L-4.\] For every fixed \(L\geq3\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), both constants are attained simultaneously by strictly positive symmetric marginals. Specifically, for any \(0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha/2,1-2\alpha\}\), the marginals with endpoint masses \((1-\varepsilon)/2\) and each interior mass \(\varepsilon/(L-2)\) have \(k^*=3\), attained by \(\{-L+1,0,L-1\}\), and \(I^*=2L-1\). Thus the interval-only oracle studied by ZhangRichardson2025 can be strictly larger by the displayed sharp factors than the arbitrary-set oracle.
body.justification: The theorem quantifies exactly how much connected reporting can conceal in the coupling-robust causal problem.
body.gap: ZhangRichardson2025 optimizes only intervals, while GaoShanSrinivasVijayaraghavan2025 compares structured sets under an observed response distribution; neither derives a sharp adversarial-coupling price.
body.consumer: For the seven-category remdesivir endpoint, a valid three-effect set can coexist with the necessity of all thirteen effects under interval reporting.
